name: ui-ux
summary: The deliverable a non-engineer can answer. Every artifact in this pack ended in a diff: /design-review reports, /redesign and /art-direct gate on written prose, design-iterate and visual-check screenshot what already renders in the app. Nothing produced a thing you send to a client, a designer or a founder and get "yes, but move that" back, and nothing at all existed for a surface that has no code yet. New design-canvas skill drafts a surface, flow or feature as ARTBOARDS on one pan/zoom canvas before any product code is written, and writes only under ai/design/canvas/ — never product source. It asks exactly one question and refuses to infer it: $SOURCE = system (lift the repo's resolved token and component literals, match exactly) vs independent (free of the repo — landing pages, greenfield). That deliberately sits beside, not against, redesign.md's rule that the language-or-composition test is never put to the user: whether our visual language is at fault is a DIAGNOSIS, an output earned from a render, and asking for it offloads work; whether this surface may leave the design system is a PERMISSION, an input only the product owner holds, and no render produces it. The skill draws the STATES — empty, loading, error, overflow — and halts on a happy-path-only set, because those are where a design is actually decided and exactly what a screenshot of a working app never shows. Two renderers consume ONE authored fragment, and the authoring targets the weaker: the static canvas (self-contained canvas.html, opens in any browser, survives being emailed) is the contract all 13 adapter tools get, while Claude Code's bundled WYSIWYG payload is an opportunistic upgrade that is pinned to the CLI build and cannot be vendored into a project — so an artboard needing holes, tweaks or a logic class is a defect, invisible everywhere else. Halts on an unresolved var() (paints as nothing, silently, in a frame with none of the app's cascade), on values rounded to a 4/8 grid instead of lifted, on recreating the app's look from memory, on LTR artboards for an RTL product, and on presenting the canvas as the change. An encodability table per surface keeps the canvas buildable: an all-empty new-work column is a restyle wearing a redesign's clothes, an all-new one is a fantasy. Wired into the two commands that gate on a proposal, because a skill nothing calls is a skill nobody runs: /redesign gains --canvas (draw the Phase-4 proposal before gating; the prose still carries the diagnosis, parity map and rationale a picture cannot state) and --from-canvas (an approved canvas IS the spec), guarded by a new Phase 4.5 canvas intake with three halts — provenance ($SOURCE must be system), scope match, and encodability reconciliation against the system as it stands now rather than when the canvas was drawn. /art-direct gains --canvas, deliberately at wireframe fidelity: structure is what is being chosen, and a hi-fi render of three directions invites picking on paint, the one axis direction-vocabulary.md excludes from the divergence check. Wiring the two surfaced a contradiction and resolved it rather than papering over it: an /art-direct direction is an independent canvas by construction, which /redesign's provenance check refuses outright — and the existing build chain already answers it, since step 1 codifies the direction into the tokens AND the idioms oracle, after which the new language IS the system. A canvas re-drawn at $SOURCE=system after codification is a valid --from-canvas input; one drawn before it is not. Re-draw, never re-label: editing a manifest to say system fakes the check instead of satisfying it. Two new hard rules in redesign.md — a canvas does not override the no-new-visual-language rule, and a picture is not a parity map.
